item.title: Wisbech man jailed following fuel station incident
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech man jailed following fuel station incident
A 27-year-old man has been sentenced to six months in prison following an incident at a Wisbech filling station last October. Lewis Marsh, of no known address, was found guilty at Peterborough Magistrates' Court of racially aggravated criminal damage, using abusive words, and possessing a knife in public.
The court heard that Marsh entered the Lynn Road premises on October 8th, where he directed racist abuse at staff. He subsequently used a knife to slash the tyres of a van parked at the site. Marsh was arrested three days later on Duke Street. Police have described the incident as unprovoked and unacceptable behaviour.

item.title: Nearly 1,000 gather in Leverington to protest asylum seeker housing plans
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Nearly 1,000 gather in Leverington to protest asylum seeker housing plans
Nearly 1,000 people gathered outside Roman Court in Leverington on Sunday to protest against government plans to house asylum seekers at the site. This marks the second consecutive weekend of demonstrations against the proposal, which aims to accommodate 26 women and children as part of a wider plan for 205 asylum seekers in Fenland.
The district council and MP Steve Barclay have formally opposed the move, citing concerns over public safety, community cohesion, and the building's condition following an asbestos-related prohibition notice. A final decision on the use of the premises is expected from the government by Friday, October 16.
🔗 More details: https://www.fenlandcitizen.co.uk/news/nearly-1-000-protesters-gathered-to-protect-women-children-9486709/

item.title: Norfolk police report 41 arrests in week-long road operation
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Norfolk police report 41 arrests in week-long road operation
Norfolk Constabulary has concluded a week-long operation targeting criminal activity on the county’s road network. Known as Operation Lockstream, the initiative saw officers focus on major routes, including the A47 near Wisbech and at Swaffham.
In total, 41 people were arrested and 40 vehicles were seized. Those detained face a variety of charges, including theft, drug offences, and immigration breaches. One stop led to the discovery of a cannabis cultivation site containing approximately 200 plants. Sergeant Josh Preston stated the operation used intelligence-led tactics to disrupt organised crime and improve road safety. The force confirmed the activity is part of ongoing efforts to prevent offenders from using local roads to facilitate criminal acts.

item.title: Wisbech farm prepares for record-breaking pumpkin harvest
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech farm prepares for record-breaking pumpkin harvest
A family-run farm in Wisbech is expecting its busiest Halloween season to date. Fen Farming, which has operated in the area for nearly 40 years, is set to supply over 500,000 pumpkins to Aldi stores nationwide.
Despite a dry summer, the farm’s silt soil and new irrigation techniques have helped protect the crop across their 800-acre site. The business has invested over £750,000 in new harvesting and washing technology to meet the rising demand. Fen Farming has been a partner of the supermarket chain since 2014, growing from an initial supply of 25,000 squashes to becoming the retailer's largest pumpkin supplier.

item.title: Looking back at West Norfolk headlines from 1994
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Looking back at West Norfolk headlines from 1994
We are looking back at the stories making headlines in West Norfolk during 1994. Plans for a two-million-pound science and technology block at Norfolk College in King’s Lynn were sent back to the drawing board after planners refused to allow protected trees to be removed. Meanwhile, the St Augustine’s Sports and Social Club in North Lynn celebrated its 21st birthday with a party for 350 members.
Elsewhere that year, Fakenham councillors raised concerns over the relocation of the town’s post office, while Lynnsport hosted a major careers convention. Additionally, Middleton Village Hall announced early plans for VE-Day anniversary celebrations, and the local NHS trust reported that hospital waiting times had been successfully reduced.
